title: Measured Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
description:
# Detailed description of the target figure: `fig_intercept_error`

## 1. Content and data mapping

**Chart type:** Single-series point chart (scatter plot). No connecting line, no fitted or interpolated curve, no error bars, no confidence bands, and no additional points.

**Variable-to-channel mapping:**

| Channel | Variable | Source |
|---|---|---|
| x-position | Added intercept correction *b* | Experimental log, column "Added b" |
| y-position | Mean squared error (MSE) | Experimental log, column "Mean squared error" |
| Color (hue) | None; one series | n/a |
| Shape | Filled circle for all points | n/a |
| Text label | MSE value at each point | Same MSE value, formatted as shown below |

**Every measured point, enumerated:**

| Point | x = b | y = MSE | Point label |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| P1 | 0 | 9 | "MSE = 9" |
| P2 | 1.5 | 2.25 | "MSE = 2.25" |
| P3 | 3 | 0 | "MSE = 0" |

**Consistency check against the log:** The residuals of the baseline (2x) are y − 2x = 3 for all five observations, so MSE(b=0) = 3² = 9. For b = 1.5, each residual is 3 − 1.5 = 1.5, so MSE = 2.25. For b = 3, each residual is 0, so MSE = 0. These match the recorded values. The correction b = 3 is the mean of y − 2x and drives MSE to zero on these same five observations.

**Scope statement:** This figure shows only arithmetic error reduction on the five observations used to determine the correction. It makes no claim about generalization, timing, or held-out performance.

## 2. Text content

- **Title:** "Measured Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections"
- **x-axis title:** "Added intercept correction *b*" (unitless)
- **y-axis title:** "Mean squared error (MSE)" (unitless)
- **Caption:** None within the plot canvas (figure caption is kept separate in the manuscript text).

## 3. Axis specification

- **x-axis:** Limits `c(-0.25, 3.25)`. Breaks at `c(0, 1.5, 3)` with explicit labels `c("0", "1.5", "3")`.
- **y-axis:** Limits `c(-0.5, 10)`, so the point at MSE = 0 is not clipped at the axis. Breaks at `seq(0, 10, by = 2)`.
- **Axis lines:** Left and bottom axis lines, 0.5 pt, color `#444444`.
- **Tick marks:** Length 3 pt, color `#444444`.

## 4. Aesthetic specification

**Colors:**

| Element | HEX |
|---|---|
| Background (panel and plot) | `#FFFFFF` |
| Major gridlines | `#E3E3E3` |
| Minor gridlines | None |
| Markers (fill) | `#1F4E79` |
| Marker outline | `#FFFFFF`, 0.6 pt |
| Title text | `#1A1A1A` |
| Axis titles | `#333333` |
| Tick labels | `#444444` |
| Point labels | `#1F4E79` |

**Typography (sans-serif, e.g., Helvetica or Arial):**

| Element | Size | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Title | 14 pt | Bold |
| Axis titles | 12 pt | Regular |
| Tick labels | 10 pt | Regular |
| Point labels | 10 pt | Regular |

**Markers:**

- Shape: filled circle (ggplot2 `shape = 21`, fill `#1F4E79`, stroke white).
- Size: `size = 4` (about 4 mm in ggplot2 units).
- Stroke width: 0.6 pt.

**Point labels:**

- Position: placed above each point and horizontally centered (`vjust = -1.1`, `hjust = 0.5`).
- Text: the MSE value as shown in the table above.

**Gridlines:**

- Major gridlines on the y-axis only, 0.4 pt, `#E3E3E3`.
- Vertical gridlines at the three b values, 0.3 pt, `#E3E3E3`, dashed (`linetype = "dashed"`), to aid reading of the x positions.

**Legend:** None.

**Plot dimensions:** 5.5 in wide by 3.8 in tall. Margins of 10 pt on all sides.

## 5. Reproducible R/ggplot2 specification

r
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
  b   = c(0, 1.5, 3),
  mse = c(9, 2.25, 0)
)

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = b, y = mse)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = df$b, colour = "#E3E3E3",
             linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 4, fill = "#1F4E79",
             colour = "#FFFFFF", stroke = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("MSE = ", format(mse, drop0trailing = TRUE))),
            vjust = -1.1, size = 3.5, colour = "#1F4E79") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 3.25), breaks = c(0, 1.5, 3), labels = c("0", "1.5", "3")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.5, 10), breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Measured Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections",
    x     = "Added intercept correction b",
    y     = "Mean squared error (MSE)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", colour = NA),
    panel.background   = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#E3E3E3", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.line          = element_line(colour = "#444444", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks         = element_line(colour = "#444444"),
    axis.ticks.length  = unit(3, "pt"),
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", colour = "#1A1A1A"),
    axis.title         = element_text(size = 12, colour = "#333333"),
    axis.text          = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#444444"),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.margin        = margin(10, 10, 10, 10, "pt")
  )


**Output artifacts:**
1. Editable R source: `fig_intercept_error.R`
2. Vector PDF: `fig_intercept_error.pdf`, saved with `ggsave(..., width = 5.5, height = 3.8, device = cairo_pdf)`
3. Manuscript-compatible preview: `fig_intercept_error.png`, saved at 300 dpi with the same dimensions.
caption: Mean squared error at three intercept corrections (b = 0, 1.5, and 3) evaluated on the five synthetic observations. The correction b = 3 reduces the mean squared error from 9 to 0 on the data used to determine the intercept.

critic_history.suggestions:
1. **Remove Embedded Caption (Rule 1 Violation & Clipping):** The figure caption ('Each point is one deterministic evaluation on the same five observations used to determine b. No uncertainty is shown.') is rendered inside the plot visual using `labs(caption = ...)`. According to the Caption Exclusion rule, figure captions must remain separate from the image visual. Moreover, this caption is visibly truncated on the right margin ('...No uncerta'). Remove the caption entirely from the plot.
2. **X-Axis Tick Formatting:** The x-axis ticks are rendered as floating point numbers ('0.0', '1.5', '3.0') rather than the specified clean tick labels '0', '1.5', and '3'. Explicitly define `labels = c("0", "1.5", "3")` in `scale_x_continuous()`.
3. **Layout & Margins:** Removing the embedded caption cleanly balances the lower margin around the x-axis title ('Added intercept correction b'), eliminating clutter and cutoff issues.

title: Residual-Based Intercept Correction on Five Observations
description:
**Canvas and TikZ Setup**
- Pure white background (#FFFFFF), borderless canvas.
- Standalone TikZ environment requiring packages: `tikz`, with libraries `arrows.meta`, `positioning`, `calc`.
- Canvas dimensions: approximately 15.0 cm × 5.2 cm, scaled compactly for single-column width (approx. 3.4 in / 8.6 cm) without text clipping or excess margins.
- Default font: Computer Modern, with math mode for algebraic symbols and variables.
- Common node style: rounded corners (2 mm), border line width 0.6 pt, minimum height 1.4 cm, `align=center`, text depth 0.25ex, text height 1.2ex.
- Arrow style: `-{Stealth[length=2.5mm, width=1.8mm]}`, line width 0.8 pt, color dark gray (#333333).
- No caption, figure title, or color legend within the visual diagram.

**Node Specifications & Layout (Origin bottom-left)**

1. **Inputs and Targets** (Top-left, center at x = 1.8 cm, y = 4.0 cm, width 2.8 cm, height 1.5 cm):
   - Fill: #EAF1F8, Border: #4A6B8A (solid, 0.6 pt).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize Observed Inputs & Targets}\\
     {\footnotesize $x_i \in \{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$}\\
     {\footnotesize $y_i = 2x_i + 3$}\\
     {\scriptsize Values: $\{-1, 1, 3, 5, 7\}$}

2. **Fixed Baseline** (Top-center-left, center at x = 5.8 cm, y = 4.0 cm, width 2.8 cm, height 1.5 cm):
   - Fill: #FBEBD9, Border: #B8702E (dashed: 3 pt on, 2 pt off; 0.6 pt).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize Fixed Baseline Predictor}\\
     {\footnotesize $\hat{y}^{(0)}_i = 2x_i$}\\
     {\scriptsize Values: $\{-4, -2, 0, 2, 4\}$}

3. **Observed Residuals** (Top-center-right, center at x = 9.8 cm, y = 4.0 cm, width 2.8 cm, height 1.5 cm):
   - Fill: #E4F2E7, Border: #3C7A4A (solid, 0.6 pt).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize Observed Residuals}\\
     {\footnotesize $r_i = y_i - 2x_i$}\\
     {\scriptsize Values: $\{3, 3, 3, 3, 3\}$}

4. **Scalar Correction** (Top-right, center at x = 13.8 cm, y = 4.0 cm, width 2.8 cm, height 1.5 cm):
   - Fill: #EDE4F5, Border: #6A4C93 (solid, 1.2 pt accent border).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize Mean Residual (Correction)}\\
     {\small $\mathbf{b = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^{5} r_i = 3}$}

5. **Corrected Prediction** (Bottom-center, center at x = 9.8 cm, y = 1.6 cm, width 3.2 cm, height 1.4 cm):
   - Fill: #E3EEF9, Border: #2F5F8A (solid, 0.8 pt).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize Corrected Prediction}\\
     {\footnotesize $\hat{y}_i = 2x_i + b$}\\
     {\scriptsize Values: $\{-1, 1, 3, 5, 7\}$}

6. **Evaluation** (Bottom-right, center at x = 13.8 cm, y = 1.6 cm, width 2.8 cm, height 1.4 cm):
   - Fill: #F2F2F2, Border: #7F7F7F (dashed: 3 pt on, 2 pt off; 0.6 pt).
   - Text (align=center):
     \textbf{\footnotesize In-Sample Evaluation}\\
     {\footnotesize $e_i = y_i - \hat{y}_i = 0$}\\
     {\scriptsize Exact arithmetic check}

**Connectors and Paths**
- **Inputs → Baseline:** Horizontal solid arrow from Node 1 right anchor to Node 2 left anchor. Centered label above arrow: {\footnotesize $x_i$}. Centered label below arrow (with 2 pt clearance): {\scriptsize (fixed map)}.
- **Inputs → Residuals (Direct Target Feed):** Controlled shallow curved arrow over Node 2, starting from Node 1 top anchor with `to[out=20, in=160]` ending cleanly at Node 3 top anchor (maximum apex at $y \approx 4.9\text{ cm}$). Centered label directly above apex: {\footnotesize $y_i$}.
- **Baseline → Residuals:** Horizontal solid arrow from Node 2 right anchor to Node 3 left anchor. Centered label above: {\footnotesize $-2x_i$}.
- **Residuals → Scalar Correction:** Horizontal solid arrow from Node 3 right anchor to Node 4 left anchor. Centered label above: {\scriptsize mean over 5 points}.
- **Baseline → Corrected Prediction:** Solid arrow leaving Node 2 bottom anchor, turning right, and entering Node 5 left anchor via an orthogonal L-path `(Node 2.south) |- (Node 5.west)`. Label along the horizontal segment: {\footnotesize $2x_i$}.
- **Scalar Correction → Corrected Prediction:** Prominent purple arrow (color #6A4C93, line width 1.2 pt) leaving Node 4 bottom anchor, dropping down vertically by 0.7 cm, routing horizontally left, and dropping cleanly into Node 5 top anchor via `(Node 4.south) -- ++(0,-0.7) -| (Node 5.north)`. Label placed to the right of the initial vertical drop segment: {\textbf{\footnotesize $+b$}}.
- **Corrected Prediction → Evaluation:** Horizontal solid arrow from Node 5 right anchor to Node 6 left anchor. Centered label above: {\footnotesize compare $\hat{y}_i, y_i$}.
- **Reuse Route:** Dashed dark-gray arrow (0.8 pt, dash 4 pt on, 2 pt off) originating at Node 1 bottom anchor, dropping vertically to $y = 0.5\text{ cm}$, extending horizontally across to $x = 13.8\text{ cm}$, and rising vertically into Node 6 bottom anchor. Centered label above the horizontal segment in italics: {\scriptsize \textit{same five observations reused for correction and evaluation}}.
caption: Schematic of the residual-based intercept correction workflow on five synthetic observations. The fixed baseline predictor 2x is compared against observed targets y = 2x + 3 to yield residuals r = y - 2x. The mean residual across the five points determines the scalar correction b = 3, which is added to the baseline predictions to obtain corrected outputs 2x + b. In-sample evaluation on the same five observations confirms exact recovery with zero residual error.

critic_history.suggestions:
1. Code Generation & LaTeX Robustness: The plot failed to render because the original description lacked explicit TikZ rendering directives. Specifically, multi-line text within nodes requires explicit 'align=center' styling; otherwise, LaTeX '\\' breaks trigger fatal compilation errors. Additionally, standard TikZ libraries (arrows.meta, positioning, calc) and explicit path routing syntax must be defined.
2. Column Width & Readability: A 16 cm wide canvas scaled down to a standard 3.4-inch (8.5 cm) single column makes small text (sub-labels and numerical sets) difficult to read.
